question: What is the primary purpose of mechanical digestion?

options.A: To change proteins directly into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid before food enters the bowel
options.C: To transport nutrients through the intestinal wall
options.D: To increase the surface area of food for enzymes

explanation: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces, which gives digestive enzymes more surface area to work on. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the main difference between mechanical and chemical digestion?

options.A: Mechanical involves physical breakdown, while chemical involves enzyme breakdown
options.B: Mechanical breaks down fats, while chemical breaks down only proteins
options.C: Mechanical requires energy from ATP, while chemical occurs spontaneously
options.D: Mechanical happens only in the mouth, while chemical happens only in the stomach

explanation: Think of mechanical digestion as the physical chewing and churning, while chemical digestion uses special enzymes to split food molecules apart. Great job learning the basics!

question: What is the name of the slippery mass of food formed in the mouth before swallowing?
explanation: The tongue and saliva combine chewed food and mucus into a rounded mass called a bolus for easy swallowing. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which nutrient starts its chemical digestion in the oral cavity?
explanation: Salivary amylase is present in saliva and begins breaking down complex carbohydrates right inside the mouth. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary movement that pushes food down the esophagus?
explanation: Peristalsis involves wave-like muscular contractions that propel food smoothly through the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the main job of the lower esophageal sphincter?

options.A: To control how fast water leaves the stomach
options.B: To release digestive enzymes into the upper esophagus
options.C: To grind solid food particles into a liquid mixture
options.D: To prevent stomach acid from flowing back into the esophagus

explanation: This sphincter acts like a one-way gate, closing tightly so harsh stomach juices don't splash up and burn your food pipe. Simple and clear!

question: Which cells in the stomach secrete hydrochloric acid?
explanation: Parietal cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor into the gastric juice. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is turning pepsinogen into active pepsin so important in the stomach?

options.A: It begins the chemical digestion of dietary proteins
options.B: It stimulates the gallbladder to release stored bile
options.C: It protects the stomach lining from hydrochloric acid burns
options.D: It breaks down complex starches into simple glucose

explanation: Active pepsin gets straight to work, chopping large protein chains into smaller pieces right inside the acidic stomach environment. Excellent!

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in digestion?

options.A: To digest complex proteins into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize the acidity of gastric chyme
options.C: To emulsify fats into smaller droplets
options.D: To stimulate the pancreas to release hormones

explanation: Bile salts break large fat globules down into tiny droplets, allowing lipase enzymes to work efficiently. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why does the pancreas secrete large amounts of bicarbonate into the small intestine?

options.A: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming from the stomach
options.B: To break down complex fat molecules directly
options.C: To turn liquid chyme into a solid fecal mass
options.D: To activate salivary amylase in the upper intestine

explanation: Bicarbonate is alkaline, meaning it cools down the harsh acid coming from the stomach, protecting your intestines and creating the right environment for enzymes to work. Well done!

question: What microscopic structures on the villi form the brush border of the small intestine?
explanation: Microvilli are tiny projections on the surface of intestinal absorptive cells that greatly increase surface area. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h6)

question: How do digested fats enter the bloodstream from the small intestine?

options.A: They pass directly into blood capillaries via active transport
options.B: They enter lymphatic lacteals before reaching the bloodstream
options.C: They travel upward through the esophagus to lymph nodes
options.D: They are absorbed directly through the stomach wall into veins

explanation: Because fat molecules are quite bulky, they first get packaged and sent into tiny lymphatic vessels (lacteals) before joining the main bloodstream later. You're doing great!

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine?

options.A: To absorb water and electrolytes from indigestible food residue
options.B: To produce bile salts needed for fat emulsification
options.C: To begin the mechanical breakdown of ingested food
options.D: To secrete strong acids and enzymes for protein digestion

explanation: The large intestine reclaims most of the remaining water, converting liquid waste into formed stool. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal function or feature of the large intestine?

options.A: Housing beneficial bacteria that synthesize vitamin K
options.B: Secreting primary enzymes to digest complex proteins
options.C: Storing waste material temporarily in the rectum
options.D: Reabsorbing water to form solid feces

explanation: Protein digestion happens in the stomach and small intestine; the large intestine does not secrete digestive enzymes for proteins. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h7)

question: What hormone stimulates the gallbladder to contract and release bile into the small intestine?
explanation: CCK is released in response to dietary fats and proteins, causing the gallbladder to release stored bile. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h8)

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect your digestion?

options.A: It speeds up peristalsis throughout the small and large intestines
options.B: It stimulates the release of bile from the gallbladder
options.C: It increases the production of gastric acid and digestive enzymes
options.D: It inhibits digestive activity during times of stress or danger

explanation: Think of the 'fight or flight' response: when you're stressed or running late for class, your body shifts blood away from your gut, slowing down digestion so you can focus on surviving! You've got this.
